headline: Global fund managers surveyed by Bank of America are almost evenly split on whether AI will become a bubble in 2027, even as they hold more technology shares than at any time since 2020.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the survey figures were read in a full account of Bank of America's survey; they show opinion and positioning, not an event.
importance_line: What changed is that professional investors are adding to technology shares while nearly half say an AI bubble could form, which matters first to savers and pension holders whose funds follow these managers, then to companies that rely on cheap AI financing, then to chipmakers named as the most crowded trade, and the doubt is that a survey of 161 managers records opinion and positioning, not what will happen.
summary: The WealthAdvisor reports that Bank of America's October survey of 161 global fund managers, who run $453 billion between them, found a net 37% holding more technology shares than their benchmark, the highest since August 2020, while 45% expect an AI bubble to emerge in 2027 and 42% do not. Long positions in global semiconductor stocks were named the most crowded trade, and a disorderly rise in bond yields, not an AI bubble, was ranked the biggest threat to markets, with 19% of allocators already moving money from stocks into bonds.
notes: Barron's page returned HTTP 401; the same Bank of America survey was read in The WealthAdvisor's full account and that outlet is credited and linked.
